messages:
han: Quick follow-up to the service auth RFC — specifically around scoping for service tokens. Do we go explicit (tenant/org/project claims in token) or implicit (actor id + routing lookup)?

maya: Short answer: both have pros. Explicit claims = safer for least-privilege checks at the edge. Implicit = simpler tokens, smaller size, easier rotation.

oliver: Performance concern with explicit claims: if we encode project list in token, validation + cache key explosion. DB lookups for delegation also become tricky.

rosie: From evals side, explicit claims let us run fine-grained audits per-project without additional lookup. But TTL & token size could hurt mobile/edge.

han: Yes. Also threat model: explicit claims leak surface if tokens are exfiltrated, but implicit requires trusted routing layer (and stronger service-to-service auth).

maya: Proposed compromise: canonical JWT contains minimal actor + aud + version, and we add an optional "scope_claim" that is signed and can be verified locally. If present, we short-circuit lookups. If absent, fall back to lookup.

oliver: That feels pragmatic. Example token payload I sketched (pseudo):
```
{
  "sub": "svc:billing:abc123",
  "iss": "redwood-auth",
  "aud": "inference",
  "ver": "2",
  "scp": "proj:proj-45:read,proj:proj-45:write"  // optional
}
```

han: Two implementation details: 1) signing key rotation for tokens with scp; 2) policy engine must accept both forms.

auth-bot: FYI: current policy service supports aud + scope checks but expects scope in DB for actor unless scp present in token. No runtime errors for either path.

rosie: Migration plan thought: introduce scp as v2 token field. When issuer issues v2 tokens, runtime treats scp as authoritative. For v1 tokens with no scp, do existing lookup. Rollout in three phases: opt-in issuers -> SDK updates (validate tokens locally) -> make scp authoritative for new endpoints.

maya: Edge-case: delegation chains (svc A acts for svc B on proj X). Need claim format that supports delegated_actor and delegation_depth or list. Otherwise ACL checks ambiguous.

oliver: Agree. Suggested claim additions: "act": "svc-b", "dl": "proj-45" (short fields to keep token small). Also add "jti" + introspection endpoint.

han: Operational concerns: cache key should include token version + jti if scp present. For implicit path, cache on actor+aud. Also need rate-limited introspection to avoid thundering herd on new tokens.

rosie: From telemetry: add histogram for path taken (scp_short_circuit vs lookup) so we can measure adoption and perf.

maya: Security review note: require scoped tokens for any cross-tenant actions by default. Internal-only service-to-service can keep implicit tokens for performance.

han: Action items: 1) maya to draft token v2 claim spec (including delegation fields) — due EOD Wed. 2) oliver to prototype runtime guards and cache key changes — start Monday. 3) rosie to add telemetry hooks to policy service. 4) I'll schedule a short follow-up sync to unblock SDKs.

maya: I also propose a minimal compatibility test: issue shadow scp in v1 tokens and ensure policy path honors it when present. Safer for migration.

oliver: +1. Small nit: ensure token size limit 4KB in proxies; otherwise mobile clients might fail.

han: Cool. If no objections I'll mark this as RFC follow-up accepted and we'll track in the auth RFC board. :thumbsup:

maya: No objections from me. :+1:

rosie: LGTM.

auth-bot: Note: created ticket AUTH-1423 to track v2 token spec and rollout.
